A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–B. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MiniGrid and Pusher experiments, including perturbation evaluations, rollout and temperature ablations, and entropy-distillation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds Ant evaluations, Pusher reward-shift results, and comparisons with action-robust baselines.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 retains the same k-nearest-neighbor entropy bonus, intrinsic-reward discounting, and cosine temperature schedule. Joint state/policy-entropy training is also retained. The additional environments apply the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds Ant locomotion with an unobservable barrier requiring hurdling, extending coverage beyond MiniGrid navigation and Pusher manipulation. It also adds continuous reward-location perturbations in Pusher; v1 tested reward relocation only in MiniGrid.

E2.justification: The Pusher obstacle comparison in Figure 5(a) adds PRMDP and NRMDP to the retained unregularized, policy-entropy, and state-entropy methods. Both new comparators appear in the plotted results and have implementation settings in Appendix B.3, introducing explicit action-robust RL comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include 200 sampled Pusher goals at each displacement radius 0.1 and 0.15, modified Ant rewards and termination conditions, and obstacle-crossing success evaluation. Added robust baselines use 256-unit networks, hyperparameter sweeps, and checkpoint selection described in B.3. These are additions; retained experiment protocols are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: Robustness analysis gains tests of continuous goal-displacement magnitude in Pusher and barrier crossing in Ant. These extend the existing robustness questions. The rollout-budget, temperature, warm-start, and state/policy-entropy distillation analyses are retained without substantive redesign.

E5.justification: Both versions report 96% confidence bounds across 25 seeds and 200 evaluation episodes for the main experiments. The added Ant figure follows this practice, and the appendix distillation plots retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. No changed empirical uncertainty-estimation procedure or repeated-run count is disclosed.

E6.justification: Figures 5–6 add substantial results for Pusher reward shifts, Ant obstacles, and action-robust comparators. Figure 5(a) reports approximately 0.02/0.03 obstacle success for PRMDP/NRMDP versus 0.37 for state entropy. State entropy also leads the added reward-shift and Ant comparisons. Retained experiments preserve their qualitative conclusions.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.7 adds Corollaries A.1–A.2 and proofs extending reward and kernel robustness bounds to empirical entropy estimates. These introduce explicit finite-state estimation-error penalties and high-probability guarantees under an occupancy-estimation assumption. v1 discusses sample sensitivity but lacks these formal extensions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: reward-robustness duality, kernel lower bounds, limitations for kernel robustness and risk aversion, and rollout-sensitive robustness to structured perturbations. Added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies the new baseline comparison: success against spatially correlated perturbations does not imply consistent superiority over robust RL methods. It also states applicability to continuous spaces under mild regularity assumptions and delineates the finite-state scope of A.7. Existing risk-aversion, sampling, and training-stability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B.3–B.4 document the added baseline tuning, checkpoint selection, goal sampling, and Ant reward, termination, entropy-feature, and obstacle settings. The code-access address changes from an anonymized repository to an identified GitHub repository; code availability was already stated in v1. Core implementation and hardware/runtime disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on f-policy gradients, multi-agent exploration, empirical-distribution concentration, and entropy continuity, plus focused positioning against action-robust RL. Most related-work discussion is retained. The new PRMDP/NRMDP discussion cites reference [6], but that entry is a recommender-system paper, leaving an attribution mismatch.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: clarified uncertainty-set wording and spatial-perturbation terminology, expanded experimental descriptions, relocation of the CVaR definition to Appendix A.6, and added acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 expands from three to four panels and adds baseline series; a new three-panel Figure 6 presents Ant results. Existing appendix figures are retained and renumbered. Table 1, the counterexample diagram, and surrounding text are repositioned, with additional title-page formatting changes.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for its retained claims. Appendix A.7 addresses the exact-versus-estimated-entropy gap in finite-state settings, while Ant, continuous reward shifts, and explicit robust-RL comparators address important gaps in empirical coverage. The mismatched baseline citation and stale ablation-panel references introduce documentation defects, but these do not outweigh the theoretical and evidential gains.
